title: Integrability and bound for a limit
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space, let $\mu$ be a measure on it, and let $F_m:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $C_m\in\mathbb R$ be given for each natural number $m$. Suppose every $F_m$ is integrable, each $F_m$ is nonnegative almost everywhere, $F_m(x)$ converges to $f(x)$ as $m\to\infty$ for almost every $x$, $f$ is almost everywhere strongly measurable, and $\int F_m\,d\mu\le C_m$ for every $m$. If $C_m$ converges to $c\in\mathbb R$, then $f$ is integrable and $\int f\,d\mu\le c$.
